# Verify and Explain: Airway case study

## Check the worked sample

```bash
Rscript scripts/R/verify_sample.R data/airway results/airway SRR1039508
```

The reference run described in the supplied guide reports **20,637,971 supplied counts** and **24,633 detected genes** for this sample. Check your exported input and saved `tables/sample-qc.tsv`; do not change a source count to make a reference value agree.

For a manual check, use an **R console** in the main folder:

```r
x <- read.delim("data/airway/gene-counts.tsv", check.names = FALSE)
qc <- read.delim("results/airway/tables/sample-qc.tsv")
sum(x$SRR1039508)
sum(x$SRR1039508 > 0)
qc[qc$sample_id == "SRR1039508", ]
```

These summaries use all supplied genes, before the fitting prefilter. The verifier independently checks only the raw total and detected-gene count. It does not validate alignment quality, the full model or the currentness of every file.

## Verify the normalized-count display

In an R console:

```r
raw <- read.delim("data/airway/gene-counts.tsv", check.names = FALSE)
size <- read.delim("results/airway/tables/size-factors.tsv")
gene <- read.delim("results/airway/tables/selected-gene-counts.tsv")
i <- match(gene$gene_id[1], raw$gene_id)
v <- as.numeric(unlist(raw[i, gene$sample_id], use.names = FALSE))
sf <- size$size_factor[match(gene$sample_id, size$sample_id)]
stopifnot(!anyNA(v), !anyNA(sf), all(sf > 0))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(v / sf, gene$normalized_count, tolerance = 1e-8)))
print(gene)
```

Exit R before entering terminal commands again. Agreement checks the saved display against raw counts and saved factors; it does not independently estimate factors, dispersions, fold changes or adjusted p-values.

## Interpret a fitted gene and the sample plots

Confirm `dex trt untrt` in the run log. Locate the selected gene in `tables/differential-expression.tsv`; record effect direction, `lfcSE` and `padj`. A small adjusted p-value is not a probability that the null hypothesis is true, a measure of clinical benefit or a guarantee of biological importance.

For PCA, state the axis percentages and distinguish paired cell-line structure from condition structure. The supplied reference figure reports PC1 47.7% and PC2 23.5%; check your own `tables/pca-variance.tsv`, which already contains percentages. Paired normalized-count lines can vary even when the fitted model estimates an overall effect.

## Your task

Write one evidence-based sentence per figure. Include a verified sample summary, a correctly directed gene estimate, a sample-pair observation and a limitation. Use source identifiers unless you have checked an annotation mapping. Cite the original study without presenting this practical as a reproduction of all its findings.

**Optional AI prompt:** “Check whether my result paragraph matches these tables, contrast and pairing. Distinguish numerical verification from biological interpretation.”
